question.text: A tower <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> of height <math><mn>60</mn><mi> </mi><mi>m</mi></math> is located exactly opposite to a tower <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> of height <math><mn>80</mn><mi> </mi><mi>m</mi></math> on a straight road. From the top of <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> if the angle of depression of the foot of <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is twice the angle of elevation of the top of <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> then the width (in <math><mi>m</mi></math>) of the road between the feet of the towers <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is

solution.text:
Let, the width of the road the road is d.

If the angle of the elevation is θ, then 

tanθ=20d, here 20 is the diﬀerence between the heights of T1 and T2.

Given that, the angle of depression is twice of the angle of elevation.

tan⁡2θ=60d

We know, tan⁡2θ=2tan⁡θ1-tan2⁡θ

∴60d=40/d1-400/d2

⇒400d2=13

d=20 3
